occurrence.window: Anchored on the first binding statewide freeze, New York Executive Order No 62 signed 14 July 2026 with an open-ended hold tied to a Department of Public Service Generic Environmental Impact Statement; Texas halted data-center approvals pending a PUCT and ERCOT audit in the week of 2026-08-03; Michigan's own moratorium question is timed to the November 2026 elections. The buildout these freezes bite into runs to the early 2030s, so the constraint operates across the whole 2 to 5 year window
occurrence.label: US states convert data-center backlash into binding permitting freezes

title: Data-center moratoria: a freeze does not delete the demand, it relocates it, and nobody has censused who gets paid for the move
thesis: Across 2026 the community backlash against data centers stopped being local politics and became binding state action. New York's Executive Order No 62, signed 14 July 2026, holds in abeyance every discretionary permit for construction or expansion of a data center consuming 50 megawatts or more, with no fixed end date: the hold runs until the Department of Public Service files a final Generic Environmental Impact Statement. Texas followed with an approval freeze pending a regulatory audit of an interconnection queue carrying more than 1,800 projects and over 474 gigawatts, more than five times the grid's record peak demand. Data Center Watch counted at least 75 projects worth about $130 billion blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 alone, roughly matching all of 2025 in three months, with active opposition groups more than doubled and spanning 49 states. Coverage reads this as an environmental and political story and prices it, where it prices it at all, as risk to the buildout. The unmapped consequence is that committed hyperscale capex does not evaporate when a state says no: it moves, and moving it has a bill. The links behind that bill are state siting and utility ratemaking (who pays for the interconnection upgrade), the consent and community-benefit apparatus, water rights and cooling constraints, environmental and permitting consultancies, and the jurisdictions and countries that win the relocated load.
why_now: Two states converted backlash into an actual construction freeze within four weeks of each other, which is the difference between a proposal and a constraint. New York's order was signed 14 July 2026 and its hold has no fixed term. Texas's freeze landed in the first week of August 2026 and is tied to an audit of a 474 gigawatt queue. The legislative pipeline behind them is already enormous: more than 300 state data center bills filed across 30 or more states in the first six weeks of 2026, with at least 18 states introducing bills that create a special electricity rate class for large energy users. And the politics have crossed party lines: Michigan's Republican Senate nominee reversed his prior position on 2026-08-20 and now backs a one-year moratorium, which is the specific occurrence this card was promoted from and the signal that the constraint is no longer one party's issue.
retail_gap: Retail exposure to the AI buildout is bought through chips, hyperscalers and power equipment, and every one of those is a well-covered trade. The moratorium wave reaches general financial coverage as a headline risk to that trade, framed as delay, and almost never as a chain with its own beneficiaries. Nobody in general coverage has enumerated the layer that gets paid when siting becomes contested: the permitting and environmental consultancies, the ratemaking and large-load tariff specialists, the water and cooling constraint, the community-benefit negotiation, or the developers and utilities in the states and countries that absorb the relocated load. The single systematic tracker of the phenomenon is a specialist research project, not a sell-side franchise, which is itself the measure of the gap.

unmappedness.rationale: The individual events are covered and one of them was national news, so this is not selection on obscurity. It is selection on the chain. Coverage treats a moratorium as a subtraction from the AI buildout and stops there. What is unmapped is the redistribution: a frozen gigawatt in New York or Texas is a gigawatt looking for a jurisdiction, and the process of finding one, permitting it, paying for its interconnection and buying its community consent has suppliers nobody has listed. Held at 68 rather than higher for two honest reasons. First, one link, the power equipment tier, is already mapped by SIG-20260828-01 and is not un-crowded. Second, the aggregate phenomenon does have a systematic public tracker, so the FACT of the wave is not hidden, only its supply chain. Held above 60 because the ratemaking and consent layer has essentially no general-investor coverage and because the relocation destination question, which states and which countries win the load, has not been asked as an investable question anywhere I found this run.

notes.text: DEDUPE AGAINST SIG-20260828-01, which is the one that matters and which the candidate row itself flagged. They separate at the question being asked, not at the subject. SIG-20260828-01 assumes the AI buildout proceeds and asks which links in its BILL OF MATERIALS are un-crowded: power equipment, grid, cooling, generation. This card assumes the buildout is contested and asks who gets paid for the PERMISSION to build: state siting law and utility ratemaking, consent and community-benefit work, water and cooling constraint, permitting and environmental consultancy, and the jurisdictions that win relocated load. Different chain, different census, opposite sign on the same event. They are NOT the same thesis and this is a new card rather than an update. The genuine hazard, stated so a chain build inherits it rather than discovers it: the two chains touch at the power-equipment link, and method section 4 names that exact failure, one bill of materials wearing three tickers is a single bet and not diversification. Whichever chain is built second must declare the shared link and refuse to count it twice.

DEDUPE AGAINST SIG-20260830-05, written in the same wave and pointing the other way. That card is a FEDERAL permitting rule that LOOSENS a constraint on on-site generation; this card is a STATE political movement that TIGHTENS a constraint on siting. The candidate record for CAND-20260830-03 already named them as the two directions of the same fight and asked that they be appraised separately, and Tally did. Kept separate here for the same reason, and the separation is real: this card's chain is consent, siting and ratemaking; that card's chain is generator, turbine and emissions-control hardware. SLATE-COMPOSITION FLAG for Ron, not a dedupe failure: two of the ten selected themes now sit on opposite sides of one fight over data-center permitting. That is defensible, because they produce disjoint issuer censuses and either can be right without the other being wrong, but it is a concentration fact the frozen slate should record rather than discover at chain time.

Taste rules applied visibly, 2 of 2 examined. TASTE-001 (no direct rare-earth-miner plays): does not bind, no rare-earth name is in this thesis. TASTE-002 (no standing macro thesis without a dated discrete event): checked carefully because this card is a WAVE rather than a single act, which is the shape the rule refuses. It does not bind, and the reason is on the card: the occurrence is anchored on a signed executive order with an exact date and an exact 50 megawatt threshold, corroborated by a second dated state action and a dated quarterly count. If this card rested on a general narrative of community opposition it would fail TASTE-002 and should be dismissed; it does not.

Anchor-date basis, since it differs from the appraisal. Tally's IMP-20260830-03 anchors this occurrence at 2026-08-20, the date of the Michigan reversal, because the candidate row carried only that top-level date. This card anchors at 2026-07-14, the day the first BINDING statewide freeze was signed, because method section 0 says an UNDERWAY occurrence anchors on the start of the shift and the shift is the conversion of backlash into enforceable law, not one candidate's position change. The Michigan event remains on the card as the why_now and as its promotion source. Both dates are exact, neither is snapped.

Venue rule applied. Tally's appraisal for this occurrence carries a listed power-equipment issuer's order book and backlog figures as its public_reach and capture_odds evidence. Those are issuer fundamentals and under the two-venue rule they resolve to data/market/ and data/edgar/ or they are NULL, so they are not carried onto this card. The Forbes article the appraisal cited for the $130 billion figure returned HTTP 403 this run, so the figure is cited here to Data Center Watch's own Q1 2026 report page instead, fetched and quoted this run, which is the primary publisher of the statistic rather than a secondary restatement of it.
